title: T7 Full Evidence Scan & Evaluation-Scope Reconciliation
purpose: Perform a fast, read-only, comprehensive inventory and reconciliation of existing T7 survival evidence before defining the next native survival evaluation operation.

OP-004.validation_basis: Task-level T7 acceptance; OP-004 overall PASS is not required because OP-004 contains unrelated task rejection.

operational_problem.value: Estimate the time from ticket Creation until the first operationally observed resolution state.

definition.value: Only information legitimately available at ticket Creation may be used as predictive input.

endpoint.value: First post-Creation History event in which Status changes to RESOLVED

event_definition.value: event = 1 when the first qualifying post-Creation Status change adds RESOLVED.

censoring_definition.value: event = 0 when no qualifying post-Creation RESOLVED event is observed through the administrative observation endpoint.

censored_duration_definition.value: Administrative observation endpoint minus Creation time

reopening_policy.value: A later REOPENED event does not replace the first RESOLVED endpoint.

re_resolution_policy.value: A later RESOLVED event after reopening does not replace the original first RESOLVED endpoint.

resolution_field_policy.value: Resolution changes are secondary/audit evidence and are not the primary T7 endpoint.

treatment.value: Preserve censored observations as right-censored survival records.

first_item_structure.value: Do not treat censored tickets as ordinary negative labels.

allowed_information.value: Fields and values demonstrably available at Creation time.

missing_value_policy.value: Unavailable Creation-time information must remain explicitly unavailable and must not be silently backfilled from current/final values.

reason.value: The target contains right-censored observations and the observed resolution process extends beyond fixed short horizons.

first_item_structure.value: Do not evaluate censored duration as if it were an observed exact resolution time.

reason.value: The prediction task is temporal and future tickets must not influence development of models evaluated on earlier tickets.

baseline_policy.value: Establish a censoring-aware non-parametric/statistical baseline before more complex predictive survival models.

candidate_model_policy.value: Progress from simple survival baselines to classical predictive survival models only after data and feature contracts are validated.

deep_learning.value: Not authorized by this contract; requires separate empirical justification after classical baselines.

scope.value: This contract freezes the modeling formulation and controls but does not freeze the final feature whitelist, exact temporal split boundary, or final model.

survival_term_hits.value: First post-Creation History event in which Status changes to RESOLVED
event = 1 when the first qualifying post-Creation Status change adds RESOLVED.
event = 0 when no qualifying post-Creation RESOLVED event is observed through the administrative observation endpoint.
A later REOPENED event does not replace the first RESOLVED endpoint.
A later RESOLVED event after reopening does not replace the original first RESOLVED endpoint.
Preserve censored observations as right-censored survival records.
Do not treat censored tickets as ordinary negative labels.
Do not assign fabricated resolution times to censored tickets.
Do not drop censored observations merely because their exact resolution time is unobserved.
Do not convert censoring into binary classification.
The target contains right-censored observations and the observed resolution process extends beyond fixed short horizons.
Time-dependent discrimination metrics where supported by the selected survival methodology
Calibration/reliability analysis where valid survival-specific methodology is available
Do not evaluate censored duration as if it were an observed exact resolution time.
Do not use ordinary MAE/RMSE across censored and uncensored records without an explicit censoring-aware justification.
Establish a censoring-aware non-parametric/statistical baseline before more complex predictive survival models.
Progress from simple survival baselines to classical predictive survival models only after data and feature contracts are validated.

sample_rows: PgUp/PgDn in editor don't move caret/cursor (platform differences)

(This bug imported from BugSplat, Netscape's internal bugsystem.  It\\nwas known there as bug #53588\\nhttp://scopus.netscape.com/bugsplat/show_bug.cgi?id=53588\\nImported into Bugzilla on 03/26/99 10:35)\\n\\nFrom the champs and it annoys me too.\\n\\nUsing PgUp and PgDn keys while composing an HTML message scrolls the\\nwindow, but doesn't move the cursor. The cursor remains where it was.  Keyboard\\nnavigation in the editor is rendered fairly useless because you hit PgDn several\\ntimes, then hit the down arrow and it takes you right back up to one line below\\nwhere you were originally.
